head.message:
fix(cli): follow Ix-pro's `ix bugs` -> `ix bug list` collapse (#396)

* fix(cli): follow Ix-pro's ix bugs -> ix bug list collapse

Ix-pro#108 deletes the top-level `ix bugs` command and re-adds its
behavior as `ix bug list`. Four places in this repo still pointed at the
old name:

- `ix workflows` printed `ix bugs --status open` in its Bug Workflow help,
  so the OSS CLI shipped instructions for a command that no longer exists.
- `PRO_COMMANDS` still stubbed `bugs`, so an OSS-only install answered
  "The 'bugs' command requires Ix Pro." — an upsell for something
  installing Pro would not provide. Commander now says
  "unknown command 'bugs' (Did you mean bug?)", which is both honest and
  more useful. The singular `bug` stub still covers the new subcommand
  form, since it swallows operands.
- CLAUDE.md and the skills output-formats reference documented `ix bugs`.

The pro-stub test loses its `bugs` rows and gains a guard that pins the
new shape: `bug list` must reach the Pro sentinel, and `bugs` must not.
Verified that guard fails when the `bugs` stub is restored.

Note: `goals` is in the same broken state already — Ix-pro removed the
command but PRO_COMMANDS still stubs it. Left alone here to keep this
change scoped to the collapse.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(cli): forward ix help bugs to the bug command

Review catch on the previous commit. Dropping the `bugs` Pro stub also
broke `ix help bugs`, which resolves topics against `program.commands`
and now finds nothing:

  Unknown help topic: "bugs". Try "ix --help" for available commands.

This is not OSS-only — `ix help` is an OSS command and post-Ix-pro#108
Pro registers `bug` but not `bugs`, so a paying Pro user hits it too.

#327 established the fix for the identical `goals` case and deliberately
kept a forwarder for it; this commit generalizes that hardcoded block
into COLLAPSED_HELP_TOPICS and adds `bugs`. `ix help bugs` now prints
the `bug` help, which documents the `list` subcommand that replaced it.

Also from review:
- The comment introduced in the previous commit asserted @ix/pro
  registers a plural for `goal` — it does not, and that exact false
  premise is what caused #384 to re-add the `goals` stub that #327 had
  correctly removed. Corrected so the next reader does not repeat it.
- `patches` was still listed as Pro-only in the skills reference, but
  #390 moved it to OSS (oss.ts registers it). An agent reading that
  reference would skip a working command.

help-topics.test.ts only grepped source text, which is how this survived;
the new test runs the real command. Verified it fails when `bugs` is
removed from the map.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(cli): anchor the help-forwarder assertion on a word boundary

Review catch on aef3b37. The `goals` row of the new forwarder test was
vacuous: `goals` is still a registered Pro stub whose own help starts
`Usage: ix goals`, which *contains* the substring `Usage: ix goal`. So
`toContain("Usage: ix goal")` passed even with the forwarder deleted
outright — it was asserting on the stub's help, not the forwarded help.

Anchoring on `^Usage: ix <singular>\b` turns three surviving mutations
into failures (delete `goals` from the map, delete `bugs` from the map,
point `goals` at a nonexistent command); baseline stays green.

Worth noting the `bugs` row was only non-vacuous *because* `bugs` is no
longer stubbed — i.e. its strength depended on the condition it exists to
protect. #384 re-added exactly such a stub for `goals`, so that is a
demonstrated failure mode here, not a hypothetical. The boundary makes
both rows independent of the stub list.

Also corrects skills/ix/references/commands.md, which still taught that
`ix patches` errors as an unknown command. #390 wired it into oss.ts and
dropped its stub; the previous text was strictly more misleading than the
output-formats line already fixed here, since it actively describes a
working OSS command as broken.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(pages): physical category pages, dead-link validation, and live smoke-test

Add physical static pages for every knowledge category (findings, evidence,
repositories, commits, PRs, issues, timeline, phases, decisions, suggestions,
files, map, contributions) so production URLs return HTTP 200 instead of 404.

Wire window.IX_VIEW in sections.js to render SPA views on category pages.
Convert root sidebar category buttons to physical links. Add KNOWLEDGE
CATEGORIES grid to overview. Fix entity index relative-link generation
(double-directory prefix for section/issue entities).

Add dead-link and placeholder token checks to validate-public.mjs. Add
verify-live.mjs production smoke-test script and a verify job after Pages
deploy in the workflow.
